claims.text: Increasing Al content in AlxCoCrFeMn promotes formation of a continuous Al2O3 surface scale.
Increasing Al content promotes formation of an adherent Al2O3 surface scale.
A continuous, adherent Al2O3 scale significantly reduces oxidation rates during sustained high-temperature exposure.
Al contents above approximately 10 at.% increase Al activity sufficiently to drive selective oxidation.
Selective oxidation at higher Al content forms a slow-growing protective alumina layer.
The protective alumina layer limits oxygen ingress.
The protective alumina layer minimizes oxide-scale spallation.
Limiting oxygen ingress and scale spallation improves oxidation resistance and maintains material integrity.
AlxCoCrFeMn alloys containing more than approximately 10 at.% Al will develop a uniform, adherent Al2O3 scale at 1000°C.
Alloys containing more than approximately 10 at.% Al will have significantly lower oxidation rates than low-Al alloys under identical conditions.
Alloys containing less than 10 at.% Al form non-continuous or non-adherent oxide scales.
Low-Al alloys exhibit higher oxidation rates and more scale spallation than alloys containing more than approximately 10 at.% Al.
The proposed Al-dependent behavior should hold near 1000°C for exposures of 100–500 hours and Al contents of 0–20 at.%.
Changes in phase stability or microstructure caused by increasing Al may independently influence oxidation behavior.

contradictions.description: Al is varied from 0 to 20 at.% while the other elements are said to be kept constant. Because atomic percentages must sum to 100%, the Co, Cr, Fe, and Mn atomic percentages cannot all remain numerically constant as Al at.% changes; only their relative ratios can remain constant.
